newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - August 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - August 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The finance ministry signed a partnership agreement with a local and international consortium on Thursday to re-engineer the government pension fund -- which has potentially significant macroeconomic implications.
- Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi accused his former right-hand man, Walter Felgate, of selling his soul to the devil by joining the African National Congress

- SA politicians found it unpleasant to be held accountable for public spending, despite their having fought for transparency during constitutional negotiations, Auditor-general Henri Kluever said on Thursday.

- Government was considering a proposal to make it illegal to build a residential home in SA without registering with the National Home Builders' Registration Council, housing department representative Brian Leveson said on Thursday.

- The SA Broadcasting Corporation's radio sport division is offering companies which buy advertising space on the perimeter fence of cricket grounds during the SA tour of Pakistan "free incidental mentions" by its commentators "wherever possible".
BUSINESS REPORT

- JCI, the country's first black-owned mining house, was to be split into three separate companies, a small corporate parent, a gold company, and a multicommodity firm, Mzi Khumalo, the company's chairman said in a letter to staff.

- Kluever, the auditor general, said on Thursday he could well take legal action against Penuell Maduna, the minerals and energy minister, as the war of words between the two escalated over alleged irregularities in the Strategic Fuel Fund (SFF).
- Consolidated Metallurgical Industries (CMI) on Thursday reported an 85 percent slump in earnings, exluding exceptional items and profits from sale of assets, for the year to June 30.
- Soekor on Thursday urged black empowerment groups to invest in the upstream oil industry by joining it in exploration and production ventures.

- If the Gauteng Gaming Board plays it cards right, residents could soon enjoy the benefits of a government owned hotel and gaming school, a convention centre at Sandton City, a Mandela museum, a "struggle" museum and a Codesa Negotiating Talks museum.
SAKE BEELD
- Auditor-general Henri Kluever, under fire from some politicians, said his detractors were targetting him because they resented having to account for their expenditure of public money.
- Rumours were circulating in financial markets that The Rembrandt Group Ltd could invest up to one billion rand to save embattled poulty firm Rainbow Chicken Ltd.
- Twenty economists participating in Beeld's "Economist of the Year" competition expects Gross Domestic Product growth this year to average at two percent.
- Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd (Implats) improved attributable earnings for the year to end June 1997 by 17 percent to 205 million rand.
THE STAR
- The pre-match hostility between South Africa and rivals Congo intensified on Thursday ahead of tomorrow's crucial soccer World Cup qualifier.

- The mother-in-law of a woman who murdered her two-year-old son by cutting his throat and stabbing him in the lungs and heart has testified that she felt as if part of her had been taken away when her grandson died.
